nodes.name: lower validation loss at a fixed budget
nodes.frame: An autoregressive Transformer language model trained with next-token cross entropy on a fixed token budget, judged by held-out validation loss.
assumptions: the model predicts the next token
validation loss on held-out text is the target
training is one pass over a fixed token budget with a fixed compute budget

nodes.name: Inputs and outputs: tied embedding, stream read-out, logits
nodes.frame: A single GPT-2 BPE embedding table (50304 x 384) is broadcast to four identical residual streams at the input, and the output head is the same table applied to a final RMSNorm of the plain mean of the four streams. Loss is uniform next-token cross entropy with no logit scaling or soft-capping.
assumptions: Input and output representations should share one matrix, so the embedding geometry must serve both lookup and classification.
The four streams should be read out by an equal-weight mean, with no learned or depth-aware read-out.
All four streams should start as copies of the same embedding rather than carrying different information.
Logits need no temperature, softcap or per-token scale even though residual RMS grows 7.8x through depth.
Rare tokens (loss 11.6 nats at rank 10k+) are handled adequately by a 384-dim tied table.
The token-frequency prior is additive in log space and unconditional.
In the baseline, row norm actually encodes output frequency (unmeasured).
Tying is kept and the input lookup keeps raw, un-normalised rows.
A per-token scale is worth having on top of a per-token bias.
AdamW lr 3e-3 is an appropriate rate for the new vectors.
An early head start persists to step 1525.
The final RMSNorm and the mean-of-streams readout stay as they are.

nodes.name: Sequence mixing: latent KV compression and expansion
nodes.frame: Keys and values are produced from a 128-dim RMS-normed latent (compress 384->128, expand 128->768) shared by all six heads, while queries come from a full 384->576 projection. The latent is a user-specified MLA substitute for V4 token compression.
assumptions: A 128-dim latent is wide enough for both keys and values of six heads at this width.
Keys and values should be derived from the same latent rather than separately compressed.
Compression is worth paying for at 1024 context where no KV-cache pressure exists.
Normalizing the latent before expansion is harmless to key/value scale.
Query projection need not be compressed, so q and kv live in different subspaces.
The 128-dim latent limits quality at 21M params, 50M tokens and context 1024. Rank is the constraint, not training time.
Spending 49k params per layer on nonlinearity beats spending them on more latent width.
Losing the linear latent at init (silu in its near-quadratic regime) costs less than the expressiveness gained.
K/V of position t should depend only on the residual at t.
K and V should share one gated code, and all six heads should see the same gate.
The effect appears within 45 steps and is concentrated on rare targets.
The gate is useful in every layer, not mainly at layer 0, where the input is the bare embedding.

nodes.name: Sequence mixing: decoupled rotary dims and QK-norm
nodes.frame: Positional information lives in a separate 32-dim rotary key shared across heads (theta 10000) concatenated to a 64-dim RMS-normed content key; queries get a per-head rotary part. SDPA scales by 1/sqrt(96) with no learned temperature.
assumptions: Content and position should be split into disjoint channels rather than entangled.
One shared 32-dim rotary key suffices for all heads and all layers.
Fixed theta 10000 is right for 1024 context and does not need per-layer or learned frequencies.
QK RMSNorm with a fixed SDPA scale gives the right attention temperature at every layer, despite max logits reaching 22.7 and entropy dropping to 0.67 by layer
No sliding window, bias toward recent positions, or attention sink is needed (first-token mass is below 0.6 percent).
Knowing the offset of the attended token improves next-token prediction beyond what head identity already implies.
The phase of a rotated content vector is decodable by `wo` plus the downstream MLP without a dedicated carrier.
The fixed geometric theta=10000 frequencies of the key path are also the right ones for the value path.
Losing content in the rotated dims of diffuse heads costs less than the offset information gains.
Every layer should get the same treatment.
Values come from the shared MLA latent, so any value-side positional signal must be injected after `expand`.
Induction heads exist by the kill step (45), so recall loss can respond.

nodes.name: Sequence mixing: head count, head structure and output proje
nodes.frame: Six heads of 64 content dims with full multi-head (n_kv_head equals n_head) causal attention over 1024 tokens; head outputs are concatenated and projected by wo, initialized at std 0.02/sqrt(24).
assumptions: Six heads of 64 dims is the right split of 384 for this depth; more smaller heads or fewer larger ones were not tested.
Every head in every layer attends over the full context with the same mechanism.
Head outputs combine by plain concatenation and a linear map, with no per-head gating or value-path nonlinearity.
GQA is unused because n_kv_head equals n_head, even though the latent already shares KV across heads.
The output projection needs no norm or scaling despite layer-0 attention gradient norm being 10x the rest.
Induction/recall is a real bottleneck at 50M tokens for this 12-layer, 21M model.
The two-layer previous-token + induction circuit uses capacity that would otherwise go to useful circuits.
A hard, fixed one-token shift is the right primitive, not a learned mix of current and previous keys.
Half the heads in every layer can lose same-token key/value pairing without hurting non-recall tokens.
Matching on a single previous token is precise enough; false matches on frequent tokens do not add noise.
The key for position j should come from the same layer's residual at j−1, not from the embedding.
The exam's fixed 1024-token windows contain enough within-window repeats (13% recall targets) to show a gain.

nodes.name: Per-token computation: SwiGLU MLP
nodes.frame: Each block has a dense SwiGLU feed-forward with hidden size 1077 (about 2.8x d_model), no biases, SiLU gating, and a down projection initialized at std 0.02/sqrt(24). It accounts for most of the non-embedding parameters.
assumptions: A single dense gated MLP per block with uniform width across all 12 layers is optimal.
SiLU gating is the right nonlinearity; sparsity or squared activations are untested.
The MLP sees only the current token's residual read-out and no local neighbor information.
Hidden size 2.8x is the right ratio given tied embeddings dominate total parameters.
Nothing in the MLP needs normalization or gating by depth despite output RMS growing to 10.9.
Absolute write RMS matters in a pre-norm stack where every read is RMS-normalized.
MLP writes, not attention writes, drive the x7.8 residual growth.
Residual growth hurts loss at 21M parameters and 50M tokens.
One scalar envelope per layer is enough; channel-level imbalance is irrelevant.
A batch-level envelope (4 sequences) is stable enough to normalize with.
The gain can be learned by the same AdamW settings as norms and embeddings.
Running statistics from training transfer to the exam unchanged (frozen EMA).

nodes.name: State across depth: four-stream Sinkhorn residual mixing
nodes.frame: The residual state is four parallel 384-dim streams; each block reads a softmax-weighted combination, runs the branch, then applies a static doubly-stochastic 4x4 mix (20 Sinkhorn iterations on exp of learned logits, init 6x identity) and writes the branch into streams with sigmoid gains starting near 1 on one stream.
assumptions: Mixing matrices should be static per block and doubly stochastic rather than input-dependent.
Four streams initialized as copies and mixed near-identity actually diverge enough to be useful.
Read weights are a token-independent softmax, so the branch cannot select streams per token.
Write gains near 1 on a single stream with Sinkhorn mixing bound residual growth, yet RMS still grows 7.8x.
Twenty Sinkhorn iterations in float32 per block per stage are a cost worth paying every forward.
The streams start as identical copies, and two of them share every init.
Exchange between streams should be non-negative and doubly stochastic, that is, diffusive.
Exchange between streams is useful at 21M parameters and 50M tokens.
The mixing is static and data-independent, with one temperature for all 24 stages.
The final readout is a plain mean over streams.
Optimiser placement and weight decay on the stream logits are neutral.
Short smoke runs can rank inits.

nodes.name: State across depth: normalization placement and initializati
nodes.frame: Pre-norm RMSNorm (eps 1e-6, learned gain) precedes attention and MLP on the stream read-out, a final RMSNorm precedes the head, and all linear weights start at std 0.02 with branch outputs scaled by 1/sqrt(2 n_layer).
assumptions: Pre-norm only, with no post-branch or output normalization, is sufficient to control residual scale.
Normalization should act on the collapsed read-out rather than per stream.
A uniform std 0.02 init is appropriate for all projections regardless of fan-in (compress, expand, rotary, head).
Scaled residual init is still the right choice when mixing weights, not plain addition, govern the residual.
Layer 0 should be structurally identical to layer 11 even though its gradient norm and entropy differ sharply.
The per-channel gains act as temperatures and not as feature selectors. In particular, the final norm under a tied head is not doing feature selection.
Muon can learn per-input-channel scaling inside `wq`, `compress`, `rotary`, `w_gate` and `w_up` as cheaply as a diagonal gain trained with Adam.
Attention sharpness is limited by the content-part temperature and not by the unnormalized rotary part.
A temperature of 1.4x is near-optimal at d_head 64 + 32 rotary dims, at 21M parameters and 1,525 steps.
Weight decay on the gains is harmful enough to matter within 1,525 steps.
The scaled branch init (std 0.02/√24 on wo/w_down) stays and does not interact with the scalars.
A learned scale is needed at every norm, not a fixed constant.

nodes.name: State across depth: layer count and block layout
nodes.frame: Twelve identical blocks are applied strictly sequentially, each with one attention stage then one MLP stage, with no parameter sharing, skip connections across blocks, or per-layer specialization.
assumptions: Twelve homogeneous blocks is the right depth; a different depth or width trade at equal parameters is untested.
Attention then MLP in alternation is the only useful ordering; parallel or fused blocks are not considered.
No block reuses weights, so depth and parameter count are tied together.
Late layers cannot read early-layer stream states except through the mixing chain.
Every token passes through every layer with equal compute regardless of difficulty.
